title: Efficient In Vivo Introduction of Point Mutations Using ssODN and a Co-CRISPR Approach
author: Levi, Sloutskin, et al.
materials: were collected and processed in parallel. Collected embryos were dechorionated in bleach for 2 minutes, and then transferred to an 1.7 ml tube. Embryos were overlaid with TRI Reagent (Sigma-Merck T9424), squished using a pestle and stored at -80°C until RNA extraction. Total RNA was extracted according to the manufacturer’s protocol. 1 μg RNA was further used for cDNA synthesis (qScript cDNA Synthesis Kit, Quantabio 95047). Quantitative PCR using SYBR green (qPCRBIO SyGreen Blue Mix, PCRBiosystems, PB20.

steps.title: Prepare homogenization buffer with Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Make homogenization buffer containing 10 mM Tris‑HCl (pH 8.2), 1 mM EDTA, 25 mM NaCl in double‑distilled water, then add Proteinase K to a final concentration of 200 µg ml⁻¹ just before use.

steps.title: Aliquot buffer into labeled tubes
steps.instruction: Dispense 50 µl of the Proteinase K‑containing homogenization buffer into each numbered 1.7 ml microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Add anesthetized fly and record data
steps.instruction: Add a single anesthetized fly to each tube (or pool up to five flies per vial if generating a final stock, scaling buffer accordingly) and carefully record any relevant information about the fly, as it will no longer be available.

steps.title: Homogenize fly with pestle or tip
steps.instruction: Squish each fly using a plastic pestle or an autoclaved 20 µl tip; if re‑using pestles, store them in ~10 % bleach, wash thoroughly before each use, and run a PCR control on a pestle‑only solution to monitor DNA contamination.

steps.title: Incubate homogenate at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the squished flies at 37 °C for 20–30 minutes.

steps.title: Inactivate Proteinase K at 95 °C
steps.instruction: Heat the tubes at 95 °C for 2 minutes to inactivate Proteinase K.

steps.title: Centrifuge tubes and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes for 7 minutes at 18,000 g and keep the supernatant.

steps.title: Use supernatant for PCR template
steps.instruction: Add approximately 1 µl of the supernatant to each 10 µl PCR reaction as genomic DNA template.

steps.title: Store crude genomic DNA (optional)
steps.instruction: The resulting crude genomic DNA can be stored at 4 °C for months.

steps.title: Perform Gibson assembly for Nup107 gRNA
steps.instruction: Carry out a Gibson assembly reaction (as described in reference [18]) to clone the Nup107 gRNA construct.

steps.title: Collect and dechorionate embryos
steps.instruction: Collect 2–4 hour embryos, age them at 25 °C, then dechorionate in bleach for 2 minutes and transfer to a 1.7 ml tube.

steps.title: Lyse embryos in TRI Reagent and freeze
steps.instruction: Overlay the embryos with TRI Reagent (Sigma‑Merck T9424), squish with a pestle, and store at –80 °C until RNA extraction.

steps.title: Extract total RNA per protocol
steps.instruction: Extract total RNA according to the manufacturer’s TRI Reagent protocol.

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA from 1 µg RNA
steps.instruction: Use 1 µg of the extracted RNA for cDNA synthesis with the qScript cDNA Synthesis Kit (Quantabio 95047).

steps.title: Set up SYBR Green qPCR reactions
steps.instruction: Perform quantitative PCR using SYBR Green (qPCRBIO SyGreen Blue Mix, PCRBiosystems, PB20.12) on a StepOnePlus Real‑Time PCR machine.

steps.title: Include no‑RT control and run triplicates
steps.instruction: Include control reactions lacking reverse transcriptase to check for genomic DNA contamination, and run each sample in triplicate.

steps.title: Analyze data by ΔΔCT method
steps.instruction: Analyze transcript levels by the ΔΔCT method using RpII18 as the internal control (forward primer AGTGATGGATGATGCGGACT, reverse primer ATGATCTCGATGTTGTCCGC); average results from four biological replicates.
